title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Internal Tools Guide
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood’s core company handbook content relevant to day-to-day employment: working culture, roles and career ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding basics, and an at-a-glance guide to internal tools and access. Intended audience: all employees, new hires, hiring managers, and people-ops partners.

1) Working at Redwood — culture and expectations

Short intro
Redwood is a developer-first, production-oriented company. We prioritize clear ownership, operational excellence, and a pragmatic approach to shipping. Our working norms emphasize asynchronous collaboration, documented decisions, and measurable outcomes.

Key expectations
- Be outcome-oriented: focus on customer impact and measurable goals.
- Document decisions: use Confluence for design docs and ADRs, link to PRs in GitHub.
- Communicate early and often: use Slack channels for signals, Confluence for reference material.
- Ownership and handoffs: team owning a service also owns its oncall runbooks and SLOs.

Working patterns and rituals
- Weekly team syncs + async updates in Confluence.
- Monthly company all-hands and quarterly OKR reviews.
- Regular game-days and postmortems for reliability work.

2) Roles & career ladders

Overview
We maintain role definitions and leveling guides to ensure promotion transparency and consistent hiring. Role families include: Engineering (Frontend, Backend, Infra, SRE, Serving Runtime), Product, Applied ML, DevRel/Docs, Design, Customer Success, Sales, and People Ops.

How ladders are structured
- IC tracks: Associate -> II -> Senior -> Staff -> Principal (titles vary by function).
- Manager tracks: Manager -> Senior Manager -> Director -> Senior Director -> VP.
- Each ladder includes: core responsibilities, success indicators, scope, and examples of work.

Promotion process (high level)
1. Candidate prepares a promotion packet: summary of impact, representative work, and manager endorsement.
2. Manager collects evidence and requests peer feedback.
3. Calibration panel (cross-functional) reviews and provides a recommendation.
4. People-ops records outcome and updates role/level in HRIS.

Resources and references
- Link to role matrix and examples: /confluence/roles/role-matrix (see related_pages).
- For questions contact: careers@redwood.com or people-ops Slack #people-ops.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Core benefits (summary table)
| Category | What’s included | Owner / Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Health | Medical (PPO/HMO options), dental, vision | benefits@redwood.com |
| Financial | 401(k) with company match, commuter/parking stipends | finance |
| Time off | 20 days PTO (pro-rated), 12 weeks parental leave, 10 company holidays | people-ops |
| Wellness | EAP, mental health sessions stipend, wellness allowance | people-ops |
| Learning | L&D stipend, conference budget (manager approval) | people-ops |

Perks and allowances
- Home office stipend for remote employees.
- Quarterly team budget for offsites and socials.
- Employee Referral Bonus: see compensation & referrals page.

Enrollment and providers
- New hires: complete benefits enrollment in the HR portal (Workday/BambooHR depending on region) within first 30 days.
- Benefits questions: contact benefits@redwood.com.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring philosophy
- High bar, fast and humane process. Inclusive interviewing practices are required for all roles (structured interviews, scorecards, and diverse interview panels).

End-to-end hiring checklist (for hiring managers)
1. Create or update role description and hiring rubric.
2. Get role approved with hiring plan and compensation range (People-ops and Finance).
3. Post role,/or engage recruiting partner.
4. Iterate on shortlists and schedule interviews.
5. Complete structured debrief and collect scorecards.
6. Offer and close; initiate background checks if required.

New-hire onboarding (first 90 days)
- Day 0: Offer accepted -> People-ops sends welcome packet, benefits link, and IT access request.
- Day 1: Orientation (company mission, org structure, security baseline), team meet-and-greet, and manager 30/60/90 plan review.
- Week 1: System access, first-priority onboarding tasks, first small deliverable assigned.
- Month 1: Complete initial learning paths (product, architecture overview, codebase walkthrough).
- Month 3: Formal 90-day review and alignment on next objectives.

Checklist for new hires (short)
- Complete HR forms and benefits enrollment.
- Complete security training and accept acceptable use policy.
- Join core Slack channels and Confluence spaces.
- Request hardware via IT self-service portal.
- Get GitHub, CI/CD, and Redwood Console access.

Manager responsibilities for onboarding
- Share 30/60/90 goals and initial small project.
- Introduce cross-functional partners and schedule knowledge-transfer sessions.
- Provide uninterrupted mentorship time during first two weeks.

5) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

Core systems and access paths
- Confluence — central documentation. Space: company-handbook, eng-*, product-docs. Mandatory for design docs and runbooks.
- Slack — primary real-time communication. Join #all-hands, #announcements, your team channels, and #people-ops.
- HRIS (Workday/BambooHR) — payroll, time-off, benefits enrollment. Link provided in welcome email.
- Okta — SSO for corporate apps. Two-factor authentication required.
- GitHub — source code and PR reviews. Teams map available in GitHub org settings.
- CI/CD (CircleCI/GitHub Actions) — pipeline docs in eng-infra.
- Redwood Console (internal) — deployments, model serving dashboards, per-route metrics. Access tiered by role.
- Internal Registry (artifact storage) — images and model packages. Use policy for tagging and retention.
- IT self-service — hardware requests, VPN setup, and software approvals.

Access request flow
1. New hire gets baseline access via People-ops initiation.
2. Manager reviews and requests elevated access through Okta Admin Console.
3. Security reviews requests defined as privileged (SRE, infra, or payment data access).

Common access SLAs
- Standard corporate app access: 24–48 hours after request.
- Privileged infra access: up to 5 business days (security review may extend).

Tooling tips and conventions
- Repo naming: team-name/service-name.
- Branching: main protected; use feature branches with PRs and required reviewers.
- Runbooks: must include owner, SLOs, and escalation matrix. Use the runbook template in eng-sre.

6) How to get help and escalate

First-line support
- For HR & benefits: #people-ops Slack or benefits@redwood.com.
- For IT/hardware: IT self-service portal.
- For access issues: submit Okta support ticket and notify manager.
- For production incidents: follow oncall playbook; page the oncall using the PagerDuty escalation policy.

Escalation matrix (summary)
1. Peer / team -> 2. Team lead -> 3. Engineering manager -> 4. Director -> 5. VP / People-ops director (for HR matters).

7) Ownership and contacts

Primary owners
- People-ops: ownership of hiring, benefits, onboarding templates (people-ops@redwood.com).
- Eng leadership: ownership of role ladders for engineering (~eng-leads@redwood.com).
- Security: privileged access reviews and SSO policies (~security@redwood.com).

Document maintenance
- This page is owned by People-ops. Reviews occur quarterly or when major policy changes occur. To propose changes, create a Confluence PR and notify the reviewers listed above.
